notes:
I've written notes for all 12 verses. One gap first: I ran out of searches before reaching netbible.org, bibleodyssey.org, the Catholic and Orthodox sites, or any prosperity / word-of-faith material, so there's no section for those. I also didn't find a real split between Protestant traditions on this chapter. The one disagreement I found is about v. 2, and it cuts across the traditions rather than following them.

**v. 1**
- The people of Jerusalem crowned Ahaziah because Arab raiders had killed all his older brothers. Guzik notes that Ahaziah turned out to be an unworthy man. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- Precept Austin cites Dillard: Jehoram had killed all his brothers and lived to see his own sons killed. Precept Austin also reads the raiders as God's discipline, fulfilling Elijah's prophecy against Jehoram (21:12–15). [preceptaustin.org/2-chronicles-22-commentary]
- In 21:17 the sons were "carried away," but here they are killed. Geisler (quoted at Precept Austin) says this is no contradiction: only the older sons were killed, and they may have been captured first and killed later. [preceptaustin.org/2-chronicles-22-commentary]
- Matthew Henry: Ahaziah is the same person as "Jehoahaz" in 21:17. The name has the same meaning; its two parts are just reversed. [studylight.org/commentary/2-chronicles/22-1.html]

**v. 2**
- **Age.** The traditional Hebrew text says "forty-two," which clashes with 2 Kings 8:26 ("twenty-two"). Guzik follows Payne in adopting 22, because 42 would make Ahaziah older than his father. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- Ellicott calls it a copying error. The Syriac and Arabic versions read 22, and Jehoram was only 40 when he died. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-2.htm]
- Keil & Delitzsch also see a copying slip, two similar Hebrew letters confused. [same]
- **Where commentators disagree.**
  - Clarke (labelled Wesleyan/Methodist on StudyLight) bluntly calls attempts to reconcile the two numbers "equally futile and absurd". [studylight.org/commentaries/acc/2-chronicles-22.html]
  - Gill (labelled Baptist on StudyLight) goes through the proposed solutions, rejects them, and concludes it is best to admit a copyist's mistake. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-2.htm]
  - Poole argues that the Hebrew phrase "a son of forty-two years" need not mean his age. It could count the 42 years of Omri's dynasty: Omri 6 + Ahab 22 + Ahaziah 2 + Joram 12. Poole also mentions a copying error as an alternative. [same]
  - JFB credits the dynasty reading to Lightfoot. [same]
  - Matthew Henry mentions a view that 42 was Athaliah's age, recorded as a reproach because she really ran things. [blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/2Ch/2Ch_022.cfm]
  - GotQuestions sets out four theories and favours the copying error. It adds that the original manuscripts were free from error. [gotquestions.org/Ahaziah-22-42.html]
- **"Daughter of Omri"** means granddaughter. Athaliah was Ahab's daughter. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-2.htm]

**v. 3**
- Athaliah, daughter of Ahab and Jezebel, made her son more a son of Ahab than a son of David. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- Guzik quotes Selman: only these two kingdoms ever had kings named Jehoram and Ahaziah at the same time, a sign of how closely Judah was tied to Israel. [same]
- Precept Austin points to Proverbs 22:6 ("train up a child"), used here in the reverse sense: he was trained in evil. [preceptaustin.org/pdf/64205/]

**v. 4**
- Precept Austin: be careful whose advice you take. "They" means advisers from Ahab's family, not just his mother. [preceptaustin.org/pdf/64205/]
- Matthew Henry: bad advice about religion can lead to foolish decisions in practical affairs too. [studylight.org/commentary/2-chronicles/22-7.html]

**v. 5**
- The Pulpit Commentary notes that Ahaziah repeated his grandfather Jehoshaphat's mistake of allying with Israel's king against Syria at Ramoth-gilead. [studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/2-chronicles-22.html]

**v. 6**
- Ahaziah went to support his wounded uncle Joram, the brother of his mother Athaliah. [preceptaustin.org/pdf/64205/]
- Whitelaw (in the Pulpit Commentary) draws a lesson about whether it is right to sympathise with the ungodly when they suffer. [studylight.org/commentaries/eng/tpc/2-chronicles-22.html]

**v. 7**
- Ellicott translates it "from God came the downtreading" (a Hebrew word used only here). He notes that Joram, Jezebel and Ahaziah all fell in one disaster, while Athaliah escaped for the time being. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-7.htm]
- Gill: it happened by God's purpose and decree, brought about by his providence. [studylight.org/commentary/2-chronicles/22-7.html]
- Geneva Study Bible: nothing happens to anyone except by God's providence. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-7.htm]
- Barnes: his early death was judgment for his idolatry. [same]
- Pulpit: "against Jehu" can simply mean "to meet" him, not necessarily to fight him. [same]
- Payne (quoted at Precept Austin): God can use the results of a sin to punish that very sin. [preceptaustin.org/2-chronicles-22-commentary]
- Wilcock (quoted by Hill) gives three causes of the downfall: false religion from abroad, family ties, and personal responsibility. [same]

**v. 8**
- Selman (quoted by Guzik): Ahaziah's brothers were already dead and their sons would have been children, so "sons of the brothers" probably means "kinsmen." [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- Guzik: Ahab was Ahaziah's grandfather, so Ahaziah fell under the judgment announced on Ahab's descendants. [same]

**v. 9**
- **The account in Kings.** 2 Kings 9:27 has Ahaziah dying at Megiddo, while Chronicles has him caught hiding in Samaria. Most older commentators combine the two.
  - Barnes and Poole: he fled to Megiddo, then to Samaria, was caught there and taken back to Jehu to be killed. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-9.htm]
  - Keil offers a different combination: caught in Samaria, shot near Ibleam, and died at Megiddo. [same]
  - Ellicott sees "a different tradition," and says such differences show the two accounts are independent. [same]
  - The Cambridge Bible thinks the Kings account is "more probably correct." [same]
  - Merrill and House are also quoted on how the accounts fit together. [preceptaustin.org/2-chronicles-22-commentary]
- **The burial.** He was buried with dignity only for the sake of Jehoshaphat, his godly grandfather. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- **"No one able to rule."** Pulpit: no one from Ahaziah's house was able to succeed him. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-9.htm] Barnes: Ahaziah was only about 23, so he had no grown son to take the throne. [same]

**v. 10**
- Jehu had wiped out Ahab's descendants in Israel, so Athaliah tried to save something for Ahab's family by eliminating David's line in Judah. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- JFB: enraged by the slaughter of Ahab's family, she resolved that David's family would share the same fate. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-11.htm]
- Kingcomments: her killing was mainly aimed at her own grandsons, the sons of Ahaziah. [biblehub.com/commentaries/king-en/2_chronicles/22.htm]
- Kingcomments also notes that Matthew 1:8 leaves out Ahaziah, Joash and Amaziah, the three generations descended from Athaliah. [same]

**v. 11**
- **The "bedroom."** Ellicott says it means the room where bedding was kept. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-11.htm]
- **Half-sister.** Several commentators (Pulpit, Benson, Clarke) think Jehoshabeath was probably Ahaziah's half-sister by another mother, not Athaliah's daughter. Benson reasons that Athaliah would never have let her daughter marry the high priest of the true God. [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-11.htm] [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_kings/11-2.htm] [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- **Wife of the priest.** Ellicott notes that Thenius doubted this detail, but Ellicott answers him and says there is "not the smallest reason to doubt it." [biblehub.com/commentaries/2_chronicles/22-11.htm]
- **The promise.** The Messiah's promised line now seemed to hang on one infant's life. [same]
- Guzik's application: God can use the courage of ordinary, little-known believers. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]

**v. 12**
- Clarke notes that the Aramaic paraphrase (the Targum) says the child was hidden in the holy of holies. [studylight.org/commentary/2-chronicles/22-12.html]
- Guzik: for David's sake, God kept his promise and spared this one survivor. [enduringword.com/bible-commentary/2-chronicles-22]
- The study notes on Bible Hub compare the six hidden years to other times of preparation, such as Joseph in prison and David in the wilderness. [biblehub.com/2_chronicles/22-11.htm]

Bible Hub also lists a Catholic commentary (Haydock) for this chapter, which I didn't open. That, plus the NET Bible notes and the Catholic and Orthodox sites, would be the next places to look.
